title: Availability computation endpoint (GET /availability)
keyConstraints: TypeScript strict, all timestamps stored and compared in UTC, slots computed on read (no persisted slots table), read-only in this task (no admin CRUD for availability rules)
description: Implement GET /availability?service_id&date, the endpoint the booking widget calls to show a customer which slots are actually bookable on a given day. This closes the gap flagged in task 001's review: booking creation currently has no concept of working hours, so without this endpoint (and the frontend wiring it enforces) a customer could request a 3am slot. Algorithm, per the design doc: (1) look up the provider's AvailabilityRule for the requested date's weekday to get base working hours; (2) apply any AvailabilityException for that exact date, which can either block part/all of the normal hours (e.g. vacation) or open extra hours (e.g. an added Saturday shift) — exceptions override the weekly rule for that date; (3) subtract time ranges covered by existing Booking rows with status IN ('pending','confirmed') for that provider on that date — cancelled bookings must not reduce availability; (4) slice the remaining free time into slots, where each slot's total size is service.duration_minutes + service.buffer_before_minutes + service.buffer_after_minutes (this matches task 001's buffer semantics: start_at marks the beginning of the whole reserved block, not just the massage itself); (5) return the list of bookable slot start times. This task does NOT include: ExternalBusyBlock / Google-Outlook sync (v2, out of scope), or admin CRUD endpoints for creating/editing AvailabilityRule or AvailabilityException rows (a separate task — for this task, assume rows already exist in the DB and are inserted via test fixtures, same pattern as task 001's Provider/Service rows).
acceptanceCriteria: GET /availability?service_id=<uuid>&date=YYYY-MM-DD returns a JSON array of bookable slot start times (ISO 8601, UTC) for that provider on that date
Slots are generated only within hours defined by the AvailabilityRule matching that date's weekday

An AvailabilityException with type='blocked' for that date removes availability for its window, even if it falls within normal weekly hours (e.g. a vacation day returns no slots, or fewer than the weekly rule would otherwise allow)
An AvailabilityException with type='open' for that date adds availability outside the normal weekly hours (e.g. an extra Saturday shift)
Existing bookings with status 'pending' or 'confirmed' on that date remove their time range (start_at to start_at + duration + buffers) from the returned slots
A cancelled booking does not reduce availability
Each returned slot reflects a duration of service.duration_minutes + service.buffer_before_minutes + service.buffer_after_minutes for the requested service
Missing or malformed service_id or date returns 400 with a clear message; a service_id that doesn't exist or isn't active returns 404
date is interpreted relative to the provider's configured timezone (start/end of that calendar day in Provider.timezone), not UTC midnight-to-midnight, even though returned slot timestamps are UTC
No slots table or cache is written — availability is computed fresh from AvailabilityRule, AvailabilityException, and Booking on every request
Response contains only slot start times — no booking ids, customer names, or other identifying details about who holds a given reserved range
securityConsiderations: This is a read-only, unauthenticated public endpoint, same trust level as POST /bookings. Validate service_id and date shape server-side before querying (avoid unhandled DB errors leaking internals). Do not return anything that identifies existing bookings or customers — only free/busy computed as open slot times. Consider a lighter rate limit than POST /bookings (this is read-only and cacheable per request, but still worth capping to prevent scraping every future date in a tight loop).
